title: Average Sydney Salary: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual pay using the 38-hour week. Includes average Sydney salary context, tax, super, and casual loading. Fair Work figures.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, annual pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52. The national minimum wage gives $52,254.88 a year before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) is the base rate for employees not covered by an award or agreement. Award rates are higher minimums set for specific industries or occupations and often include penalty rates, allowances, and overtime. Most employees are covered by an award, so their minimum pay is likely above the national minimum wage.

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied in the calculator?
faqs.a: The calculator has a checkbox that adds 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate you enter. For example, if your base rate is $26.44, ticking casual loading gives $33.05 per hour. You should never type a rate that already includes casual loading; let the calculator add it for you.

faqs.q: Does the annual figure include super and tax?
faqs.a: No. The annual figure shown is gross pay before tax and before super. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings and is paid on top of the gross amount, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is then calculated on the gross figure using the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the Medicare levy. The final take-home estimate deducts tax and Medicare only.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to convert your hourly rate to annual pay

To work out your annual pay from an hourly rate, multiply the hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. The standard full-time week in Australia is 38 hours, so the formula becomes:

**Hourly rate × 38 × 52 = annual gross pay**

For example, the national minimum wage of $26.44 per hour gives:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,254.88 per year

If you work a different number of hours each week, use your actual average. The calculator on this site assumes a consistent 38-hour week unless you change it. You can also see the fortnightly amount by doubling the weekly figure – for the minimum wage that’s $2,009.80 every two weeks.

## What the annual figure includes and excludes

The annual pay shown is your gross income before tax and before super. It assumes the same hourly rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. This is an estimate, not a determination of your actual pay.

### National Minimum Wage vs award rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the national minimum wage. From 1 July 2026 it is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, or $1,004.90 per week. Casual employees get a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. However, most employees are covered by an award or registered agreement that sets higher minimum rates. Award rates vary by industry and classification and often include penalty rates for weekends, nights, and overtime. Always check the relevant award or use the Fair Work Ombudsman’s Pay Calculator to find your correct minimum.

### Casual loading

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base rate. The calculator has a checkbox that adds this loading automatically. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading – let the tool do the calculation. For award-covered casuals, the loading may already be built into the award rate, so check your award first.

## The average Sydney salary in context

When people search for the “average Sydney salary”, they often want a benchmark for full-time earnings. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports that for May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings averaged $2,083.70 per week nationally. That works out to about $108,352 per year. For all employees (including part-time), the average weekly total earnings were $1,579.20, or roughly $82,118 annually.

Sydney salaries tend to be higher than the national average due to the cost of living and industry mix, but the ABS does not publish a separate Sydney figure in this release. Using the national full-time average gives a reasonable starting point. If your hourly rate is around $55, you would be close to that average. The calculator lets you compare your own rate against these benchmarks.

## Super and tax on your annual pay

### Super guarantee

Your employer must pay superannuation on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% from 1 July 2026, and it is paid on your ordinary time earnings (including casual loading if applicable). Super is not deducted from your pay – it is an extra contribution. The maximum earnings base for super is $270,830 per year; earnings above that do not attract compulsory super.

### Tax and Medicare

Your annual gross pay is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income over $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. The calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds for the levy because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this tool’s update. HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not included.

### Example: minimum wage take-home

For the national minimum wage annual figure of $52,254.88:
- Tax: $0 on first $18,200, then 15% on $26,800 = $4,020, then 30% on $7,254.88 = $2,176.46, total tax $6,196.46
- Medicare levy: 2% of $52,254.88 = $1,045.10
- Take-home pay: $52,254.88 – $6,196.46 – $1,045.10 = $45,013.32 per year (about $865.64 per week)

Super would be an extra $6,270.59 paid on top (12% of $52,254.88).

## Using the timesheet and other tools

To get your own estimate, start at [the timesheet](/). Enter your base hourly rate, select your hours per week (default 38), and tick the casual loading box if it applies. The calculator will show your annual gross, fortnightly, weekly, and hourly breakdowns, plus estimated tax, Medicare, and super. For more detail on award rates, visit the [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data). You can also read about [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage), [take-home pay](/topics/take-home), and [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

Remember: this is an estimate. Your actual pay may differ due to overtime, penalties, allowances, or salary sacrifice. Always check your award or agreement and consult a tax professional for personal advice.
